checked_sources.source: Saha & Ramdas 2026, Non-partitioned e-detectors for nonparametric sequential change detection, arXiv:2607.28322v1, Section 5.2
checked_sources.result: Primary-source HTML verification. The full-Gaussian point-null martingale has log form log C_s+n_s A(eta)-eta_1 S_s-eta_2 Q_s in Gaussian natural parameters eta_1=theta/r, eta_2=-1/(2r). The all-start objective is smooth convex in two dimensions, requires O(t) active starts, and Theorem 5.3 attains high-probability late-change delay log A/D_KL(Q||P) by using the pure post-change summand on a compact neighborhood of P and the prefix-crossing summand outside it.

derived_results.claim: For the full-Gaussian detector, the two-start pathwise-lower minimax can be reduced from a two-dimensional convex optimization over candidate mean/variance to a one-dimensional concave maximization over a mixing weight lambda in [0,1].
derived_results.derivation: Let f_i(eta)=log L_i^eta for the short and prefix intervals. Because log is monotone, log inf_eta max{L_0^eta,L_1^eta}=inf_eta max{f_0(eta),f_1(eta)}. Write max{x,y}=sup_{lambda in [0,1]}{lambda x+(1-lambda)y}. The f_i are closed convex and coercive on the Gaussian natural-parameter domain for nondegenerate interval statistics, so convex minimax/strong duality yields inf_eta max_i f_i = sup_lambda inf_eta {lambda f_0(eta)+(1-lambda)f_1(eta)}. Even without invoking equality, weak duality makes every evaluated lambda a certified lower bound, which is enough for exact false-alarm safety.

derived_results.claim: The inner optimization in the pair dual has a closed-form Gaussian fit to fractional pooled sufficient statistics, so each lambda score costs O(1) once per-start summaries are maintained.
derived_results.derivation: From the source representation f_i(eta)=log C_i+n_i A(eta)-eta_1 S_i-eta_2 Q_i, define n_lambda=lambda n_0+(1-lambda)n_1, S_lambda=lambda S_0+(1-lambda)S_1, Q_lambda=lambda Q_0+(1-lambda)Q_1, and c_lambda=lambda log C_0+(1-lambda)log C_1. The weighted objective is c_lambda+n_lambda A(eta)-eta_1 S_lambda-eta_2 Q_lambda. Its minimizer is the Gaussian MLE for the pseudo-moments: m_lambda=S_lambda/n_lambda and v_lambda=Q_lambda/n_lambda-m_lambda^2. When v_lambda>0, the minimized value is h(lambda)=c_lambda+(n_lambda/2){1+log(2 pi v_lambda)}. Therefore the exact pair log-certificate is sup_{lambda in [0,1]}h(lambda); h is concave because it is an infimum of functions affine in lambda. Any finite set of lambda evaluations provides a pathwise-safe lower certificate max h(lambda_j), and adaptive scalar maximization can improve power without ever risking an upward approximation to the exact pair infimum.
derived_results.edge_cases: If a fractional pooled variance reaches zero for a tiny/degenerate interval, retain a conservative lower value or delay use of that pair until nondegenerate; Gaussian continuous data make exact degeneracy probability zero for ordinary block sizes.

derived_results.claim: Combining the one-dimensional dual pair score with the configurable recycled K-grid gives pathwise-valid O(K log t) active-state full-Gaussian monitoring and high-probability late-change delay factor r_K=(2K+1)/(2K-1) on the instance-specific KL scale D_KL(Q||P).
derived_results.derivation: Keep the prefix start and K-grid trailing starts. For each pair use the exact dual supremum, or a certified lower approximation. Pathwise each pair minimax is below the full all-start detector. At t=T+D with D=r_K(1+epsilon)L/I_G, the grid provides a pure post block g>=c_K D. Theorem 5.3's proof applies verbatim to that short block on a compact neighborhood U of P, where uniform log growth is g(I_G-2eta), while the prefix block controls U^c at order T. Thus the pair score crosses with probability tending to one. Slowly growing K_A makes the high-probability factor approach one while active per-start state remains polylogarithmic in history.
derived_results.scope: New synthesis/derivation. It inherits the source's high-probability asymptotic regime and instance-specific Gaussian KL scale. Expected CADD still requires explicit finite-block tail amplification. Numerical implementations must only threshold lower-certified lambda maxima; a converged optimizer value without certification is not automatically safe.

candidates_new.mechanism: Use two-start minimax duality to collapse full Gaussian composite-null pair evidence to scalar lambda optimization over fractionally pooled sufficient statistics, then apply the configurable recycled K-grid and permanent prefix anchor.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: Source full detector: O(t) active starts and two-dimensional convex objective evaluations; source delay denominator is exact D_KL(Q||P). Derived sparse version: O(K log t) active starts, O(1) score work per lambda evaluation, exact/pathwise false-alarm domination, and high-probability delay factor r_K=(2K+1)/(2K-1).
candidates_new.scope: Derived, not peer-reviewed. Scalar lambda iteration count and finite-CADD tails are separate engineering/theory frontiers.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Degenerate pooled variance needs safe fallback; aggressive approximate lambda maximization is fine only because sampled lambda values are lower bounds, but claiming the exact pair value requires convergence/duality conditions; predictor summaries must remain correctly tied to each recycled start.
candidates_new.confidence: high for weak-dual safe lower scoring and Gaussian inner closed form; medium-high for strong-dual exactness under nondegeneracy/coercivity; medium-high for high-probability delay adaptation

generalization_hypothesis.statement: The pair-dual trick is not Gaussian-specific: for exponential-family point-null likelihood-ratio/e-process blocks with log form c_i+n_i A(eta)-eta dot T_i, two-start minimax evidence reduces to a scalar lambda outer problem whose inner minimization is the convex conjugate of A at fractionally pooled sufficient statistics.
generalization_hypothesis.status: mathematically plausible derived generalization; not separately source-verified here
generalization_hypothesis.potential_value: Turns a d-dimensional composite-null pair optimization into one-dimensional evidence mixing while preserving pathwise lower-certificate semantics.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The two-dimensional natural-parameter Newton solve is unavoidable even after reducing to only two starts.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: No for Gaussian pairs. Weighted-minimax duality analytically eliminates the natural parameters at each lambda via pooled mean/variance.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Use scalar lambda search and treat every evaluated lambda as a certified lower bound.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: A lower-certified lambda approximation must have a numerical proof of closeness before it is safe to threshold.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: No. Any feasible lambda gives a dual lower bound and is false-alarm safe immediately; closeness matters only for statistical power/delay, not validity.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: This cleanly separates numerical convergence from type-I safety.

frontier: Differentiate h(lambda) and derive a bracketed scalar maximizer with explicit additive suboptimality bounds; quantify the lambda evaluations needed for an o(log A) power loss so the source leading delay constant is retained numerically.
Prove strong duality including small-block/coercivity boundary cases, or retain weak-dual scoring as the formally guaranteed implementation and state exactness only under verified nondegeneracy.
Derive finite-block exponential lower tails for Gaussian predictive log scores so disjoint-block retry amplification can upgrade cf-g1-r59 from high-probability delay to CADD.
Test the general exponential-family pair dual on Poisson/Bernoulli natural families and determine whether the scalar dual certificate subsumes the bounded-mean KL pair frontier.
Resume off-policy predictable-prior/vector evidence after the Gaussian finite-tail question is resolved or bounded.

actions_taken_instead_of_stopping: Moved from studentized mean-null monitoring to the source's stronger instance-specific full-Gaussian detector.
Eliminated the two-dimensional candidate-null pair optimization by convex duality and pooled sufficient statistics.
Separated weak-dual lower certification, which is immediately safe, from exact strong-dual equality, which needs regularity.
Recovered the configurable-grid high-probability compute-delay curve on the full Gaussian KL scale.

exact_next_action: Derive h'(lambda) and a certified scalar bracketing rule whose best sampled lambda is always a safe lower certificate and whose additive gap is o(log A), then use Gaussian concentration of pooled mean/variance/predictive scores to seek retry-amplified CADD on the full D_KL scale.
